+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Copy a packaged steam.desktop, rewriting every Exec=/usr/bin/steam to a wrapper.
+#
+#   steam-desktop-override <src> <dst> <wrapper>
+#
+# Called from home.nix's steamDesktopOverride activation entry, which passes
+# /usr/share/applications/steam.desktop, ~/.local/share/applications/steam.desktop
+# and the `steam` wrapper it builds. See the wrapper's comment in home.nix for why
+# Steam needs to be launched through one at all.
+#
+# A script here, rather than the whole file mirrored into home.nix the way
+# Zoom.desktop is: steam.desktop is ~400 lines -- Comment= in 27 languages, then
+# nine Desktop Actions each with its own set -- and the only lines that need to
+# differ are the ten Exec=. Deriving the file from the pacman one also means a
+# steam.desktop changed by a package update is picked up by the next `hms` instead
+# of silently drifting from a copy in this repo.
+#
+# An unreadable source is success, not failure. That keeps "which hosts have
+# Steam" a question only system/packages.<host> answers -- the same split
+# system/thermald-setup uses for its own enable half -- so this can run
+# unconditionally on every host, including the Darwin one, and do nothing.
+set -eu
+
+src=${1:?source desktop file}
+dst=${2:?destination desktop file}
+exe=${3:?wrapper to point Exec= at}
+
+[ -r "$src" ] || exit 0
+
+# Two anchored patterns rather than one with \b, which is a GNU sed extension:
+# activation runs on Darwin too, and while the readable-source check above means
+# sed is never reached there today, a pattern that only works under GNU sed is a
+# trap for whoever moves this next. Anchoring also does the job \b was for --
+# neither matches a hypothetical Exec=/usr/bin/steamfoo.
+mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dst")"
+tmp=$(mktemp "$dst.XXXXXX")
+trap 'rm -f "$tmp"' EXIT
+
+sed -e "s|^Exec=/usr/bin/steam |Exec=$exe |" \
+    -e "s|^Exec=/usr/bin/steam\$|Exec=$exe|" \
+    "$src" > "$tmp"
+
+# 0644 explicitly: mktemp makes it 0600, and a desktop file the launcher cannot
+# read is the same as no override at all.
+chmod 0644 "$tmp"
+mv -f "$tmp" "$dst"
+trap - EXIT

+#   xdg-user-dir: symbol lookup error: /usr/lib/libc.so.6: undefined symbol:
+#   __pointer_chk_guard, version GLIBC_PRIVATE

+# Steam shells out to `xdg-user-dir DOWNLOAD` to find the download directory.
+# `~/.nix-profile/bin` sits ahead of `/usr/bin`, and xdg.userDirs.enable puts
+# nix's xdg-user-dirs in the profile, so that resolves to the nix binary -- which
+# Steam's runtime then forces against the host's /usr/lib/libc.so.6, a glibc that
+# does not export the GLIBC_PRIVATE symbol a nix-glibc build wants. The wrapper
+# puts the host's own helpers first so Steam gets /usr/bin/xdg-user-dir.
+#
+# The half that is easy to get wrong is the other direction, which is why it has
+# cases of its own: the profile must NOT be dropped from PATH. `xdg-open` exists
+# ONLY in the nix profile on this box (Arch's xdg-utils is not installed), and it
+# is how Steam opens a link in a browser. A wrapper that sanitised PATH by
+# stripping nix would trade a broken download path for broken links.
+#
+#   ./tests/steam-env.sh                 # builds the wrapper, then tests it
+#   ./tests/steam-env.sh /path/to/steam  # tests one you already have
+#
+# The wrapper is resolved from homeConfigurations.shiori specifically, not from
+# $(cat /etc/hostname): steam is a shiori-only package, and the cases are about

+# the one box.

+echo "PATH=$PATH"
+echo "GIO_EXTRA_MODULES=${GIO_EXTRA_MODULES-<unset>}"
+echo "GIO_MODULE_DIR=${GIO_MODULE_DIR-<unset>}"
+echo "XDG_DATA_DIRS=${XDG_DATA_DIRS-<unset>}"

+else
+  echo "$fails of $n cases FAILED"
+fi

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Copy a packaged steam.desktop, rewriting every Exec=/usr/bin/steam to a wrapper.
+#
+#   steam-desktop-override <src> <dst> <wrapper>
+#
+# Called from home.nix's steamDesktopOverride activation entry, which passes
+# /usr/share/applications/steam.desktop, ~/.local/share/applications/steam.desktop
+# and the `steam` wrapper it builds. See the wrapper's comment in home.nix for why
+# Steam needs to be launched through one at all.

+# A script here, rather than the whole file mirrored into home.nix the way
+# Zoom.desktop is: steam.desktop is ~400 lines -- Comment= in 27 languages, then
+# nine Desktop Actions each with its own set -- and the only lines that need to
+# differ are the ten Exec=. Deriving the file from the pacman one also means a
+# steam.desktop changed by a package update is picked up by the next `hms` instead
+# of silently drifting from a copy in this repo.
+#
+# An unreadable source is success, not failure. That keeps "which hosts have
+# Steam" a question only system/packages.<host> answers -- the same split
+# system/thermald-setup uses for its own enable half -- so this can run
+# unconditionally on every host, including the Darwin one, and do nothing.
+set -eu
+
+src=${1:?source desktop file}
+dst=${2:?destination desktop file}
+exe=${3:?wrapper to point Exec= at}

+# activation runs on Darwin too, and while the readable-source check above means
+# sed is never reached there today, a pattern that only works under GNU sed is a
+# trap for whoever moves this next. Anchoring also does the job \b was for --
+# neither matches a hypothetical Exec=/usr/bin/steamfoo.

+    -e "s|^Exec=/usr/bin/steam\$|Exec=$exe|" \
+    "$src" > "$tmp"

+# read is the same as no override at all.
+chmod 0644 "$tmp"
+mv -f "$tmp" "$dst"
+trap - EXIT

+    bad "rewrite succeeds and creates the destination directory" "$(sed 's/^/      /' "$D/err")"
+  fi
+
+  chk() { # chk <case> <expected exact line>
+    if grep -qxF "$2" "$out" 2>/dev/null; then ok "$1"
+    else bad "$1" "    wanted: $2"; fi
+  }
+  chk "main Exec= is rewritten, %U kept"        "Exec=$W %U"
+  chk "an action's steam:// argument is kept"   "Exec=$W steam://store"
+  chk "a bare Exec= with no argument is rewritten" "Exec=$W"
+  chk "a translated Name= is untouched"         "Name[uk]=Крамниця"
+  chk "a translated Comment= is untouched"      "Comment[ja]=Steam 上でゲームを管理＆プレイするためのアプリケーション"
+
+  # Anchoring earns its keep twice: a key that merely ends in the same path, and a
+  # binary whose name merely starts with "steam".
+  chk "X-Not-Exec= is not rewritten"            "X-Not-Exec=/usr/bin/steam %U"
+  chk "Exec=/usr/bin/steamfoo is not rewritten" "Exec=/usr/bin/steamfoo --wat"
+
+  # Nothing but Exec= may move. This is the case that would catch a future pattern
+  # widened past what it meant to touch.
+  changed=$(diff "$D/steam.desktop" "$out" | grep '^[<>]' | grep -cv '^[<>] Exec=/usr/bin/steam\|^[<>] Exec=/nix/store/fake-steam' || true)
+  if [ "$changed" = 0 ]; then ok "no line other than an Exec= differs"
+  else bad "no line other than an Exec= differs" "$(diff "$D/steam.desktop" "$out" | sed 's/^/      /')"; fi
+
+  # The launcher runs as this user but reads the file like any other; mktemp's 0600
+  # would leave an override that silently does not apply under some launchers.
+  mode=$(stat -c '%a' "$out" 2>/dev/null || echo "?")
+  if [ "$mode" = 644 ]; then ok "the override is mode 0644"
+  else bad "the override is mode 0644" "    got $mode"; fi
+
+  # The host gate. Every host runs this activation entry, so a box without Steam --
+  # or the Darwin one -- must come out clean and quiet, not failed.
+  rm -f "$D/absent.desktop"
+  if bash "$OVERRIDE" "$D/absent.desktop" "$D/never" "$W" 2>"$D/err2"; then
+    if [ ! -e "$D/never" ] && [ ! -s "$D/err2" ]; then
+      ok "an unreadable source exits 0, writes nothing, says nothing"
+    else
+      bad "an unreadable source exits 0, writes nothing, says nothing" \
+        "    created: $([ -e "$D/never" ] && echo yes || echo no), stderr: $(cat "$D/err2")"
+    fi
+  else
+    bad "an unreadable source exits 0, writes nothing, says nothing" "    exited non-zero"
+  fi
+
+  # Re-running over an existing override is what every `hms` after the first does.
+  before=$(cat "$out")
+  bash "$OVERRIDE" "$D/steam.desktop" "$out" "$W" 2>/dev/null
+  if [ "$before" = "$(cat "$out")" ]; then ok "re-running is idempotent"
+  else bad "re-running is idempotent" "    second run changed the file"; fi
+
+  # No temp file may survive next to the real one; a launcher scanning the
+  # directory would pick up steam.desktop.XXXXXX as a second entry.
+  leftovers=$(find "$(dirname "$out")" -name 'steam.desktop.*' | wc -l)
+  if [ "$leftovers" = 0 ]; then ok "no mktemp leftovers beside the override"
+  else bad "no mktemp leftovers beside the override" "    found $leftovers"; fi
+fi
+
+echo
+[ "$skips" -gt 0 ] && echo "$skips skipped"
+if [ "$fails" -eq 0 ]; then
+  echo "all $n cases passed"
+else
+  echo "$fails of $n cases FAILED"
+fi
+exit $((fails > 0))

hms = pkgs.writeShellScriptBin "hms" ''
    set -euo pipefail

    repo="$HOME/devel/dotfiles"
    host="$(uname -n)"
    forge="https://forge.ko.ag"
    slug="sauyon/dotfiles"
    curl=${lib.getExe pkgs.curl}
    jq=${lib.getExe pkgs.jq}

    local_only=0
    hm_args=()
    for a in "$@"; do
      case "$a" in
        -l|--local) local_only=1 ;;
        -h|--help)
          echo "usage: hms [--local] [home-manager switch args...]"
          echo "  default: push HEAD, wait for its CI run, then switch (a download)"
          echo "  --local: skip CI and build here"
          exit 0 ;;
        *) hm_args+=("$a") ;;
      esac
    done

    switch_now() {
      exec home-manager switch --flake "$repo#$host" ''${hm_args[@]+"''${hm_args[@]}"}
    }

    # mari (darwin) has no Linux CI job; nix-home.yml builds only these.
    case "$host" in
      utsuho|setsuna|fujiwara|shiori) ;;
      *) echo "hms: $host has no CI job — switching locally" >&2; switch_now ;;
    esac

        success|failure|cancelled|skipped) break ;;
      esac
      if [ "$SECONDS" -ge "$deadline" ]; then
        echo "hms: run $run still ''${status:-unknown} after an hour — giving up on the wait." >&2
        echo "hms: check $forge/$slug/actions/runs/$run, or 'hms --local'." >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      sleep 15
    done

    if [ "$status" = "success" ]; then
      echo "hms: run $run green — switching (should be a download)"
      switch_now
    fi

    echo "hms: run $run $status" >&2
    # Forgejo 13 exposes no run->job API, but the web job endpoint names the job
    # id in its error body, and /actions/jobs/<id>/logs then serves the log.
    job=$(api_raw "/$slug/actions/runs/$run/jobs/0" -X POST \
            -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"logCursors":[]}' \
          | ${lib.getExe pkgs.gnugrep} -o 'job_id [0-9]*' | tr -dc '0-9' || true)
    if [ -n "$job" ]; then
      log="$tmp/job.log"
      if ! api "/api/v1/repos/$slug/actions/jobs/$job/logs" > "$log"; then
        # Printing "--- CI error ---" over an empty file would read as "the run
        # failed silently", which is a different and much more alarming bug.
        echo "hms: could not fetch the job log: $(api_why)" >&2
        echo "hms: read it at $forge/$slug/actions/runs/$run" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      echo "--- CI error ---" >&2
      # Timestamps are a fixed 29-char prefix; drop them so the errors read.
      # A pipeline's status is its last command, so grep's miss has to be
      # captured rather than tested through `cut | tail`.
      errs=$(${lib.getExe pkgs.gnugrep} -aE "^.{29}(error:|.*Job failed)" "$log" || true)
      if [ -n "$errs" ]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$errs" | cut -c30- | tail -30 >&2
      else
        tail -30 "$log" | cut -c30- >&2
      fi
    fi
    echo "hms: not switching. Fix CI, or 'hms --local' to build here." >&2
    exit 1
  '';

  claude-prof = pkgs.writeShellScriptBin "claude-prof" ''
    set -euo pipefail
    CONFIG_HOME="''${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}"

  home.activation.piModelsConfig = lib.hm.dag.entryAfter [ "writeBoundary" "sops-nix" ] ''
    DEST="$HOME/.pi/agent/models.json"
    TMPL="${modelsTemplate}"
    KEY_FILE="$HOME/.config/local-auto-mode/api-key"
    $DRY_RUN_CMD mkdir -p "$HOME/.pi/agent"
    if [ -r "$KEY_FILE" ]; then

        '.providers.modular.apiKey = ($key | sub("\n$"; ""))' \
        "$TMPL" > "$DEST.new"
      $DRY_RUN_CMD mv "$DEST.new" "$DEST"
      $DRY_RUN_CMD chmod 0600 "$DEST"
    else
      # No key: still write the providers so `pi --list-models` shows them and
      # says they are unauthenticated, rather than pi seeing no provider at all.
      $DRY_RUN_CMD cp "$TMPL" "$DEST"
      $DRY_RUN_CMD chmod 0644 "$DEST"
    fi

  # this file (`theme`, `lastChangelogVersion`), so rendering it from a template
  # — or `force`-ing a home.file over it — would reset them at every switch and

  # subtree IS replaced wholesale (see `piRetry` above) so a stale hand-edit of

  # key here and fails at the first turn.

    DEST="$HOME/.pi/agent/settings.json"

# Error-handling / robustness review — steam wrapper + steam-desktop-override

Files: `/home/sauyon/devel/dotfiles/.drovr/wt/steam-nix-env/home.nix` (wrapper at 493–536, activation entry at 1956–1962, package list ~2431), `/home/sauyon/devel/dotfiles/.drovr/wt/steam-nix-env/home/steam-desktop-override`, `/home/sauyon/devel/dotfiles/.drovr/wt/steam-nix-env/tests/steam-env.sh`, `/home/sauyon/devel/dotfiles/.drovr/wt/steam-nix-env/README.md`.

Ground truth I verified rather than assumed, from the pinned home-manager source `/nix/store/REDACTED`:

- `modules/home-environment.nix:820` — the generated `activate` starts `set -eu` + `set -o pipefail`. Any non-zero exit from an activation entry kills the rest of the script.
- `home-manager/home-manager:829` — for `switch`, the CLI runs `nix-env --profile .../home-manager --set "$generation"` **before** `"$activateScript" --driver-version 1 || return`.
- `modules/home-environment.nix:873` and `modules/lib-bash/activation-init.sh:63` — the `gcroots/current-home` link (which is where `oldGenPath` comes from) is written only at the **end** of `activate`, and the temporary `new-home` root is removed by an EXIT trap.
- `modules/lib-bash/activation-init.sh:151-160` — `DRY_RUN_CMD=echo` under dry-run, `""` otherwise; the variable is documented as deprecated in favour of `run`.
- Sibling ordering under `writeBoundary` is decided by the topo-sort's attribute order. Confirmed empirically against a real built generation, `/nix/store/REDACTED/activate`: `linkGeneration` → `antigravitySettingsSeed` → `installPackages` → `onFilesChange` → `sops-nix` → `opencodeConfig` → … → `reloadSystemd` → `zen-browser-default` → `zenInstallsIni`. `steamDesktopOverride` sorts after `reloadSystemd` and **before** `zen-browser-default` / `zenInstallsIni`.
- The real `/usr/share/applications/steam.desktop` on this box has exactly 10 `Exec=/usr/bin/steam …` lines (1 main + 9 actions), all matching one of the two patterns; `/usr/bin/steam` is `#!/bin/sh` + `exec /usr/lib/steam/steam "$@"`, so there is no re-exec-by-name recursion hazard.
- `~/.local/share/applications` is a real directory containing hm store symlinks (`Zoom.desktop`, `mimeapps.list`), not itself a store symlink.

---

## Critical

**C1. A cosmetic launcher tweak can abort the whole switch, and the resulting state is not "nothing happened" — it is "switched, but the generation bookkeeping disagrees and two later entries were skipped".**

Trigger: any non-zero exit from `home/steam-desktop-override` — `mkdir -p` failing (`~/.local/share` read-only, quota exhausted, `applications` turned into a store symlink by some future `home.file` entry with a directory source), `mktemp` failing (ENOSPC / EDQUOT / EACCES), `sed` failing to flush (ENOSPC), `mv` failing. Also any future non-zero path added to the script.

Because `set -eu` is on in `activate` and `steamDesktopOverride` sorts *after* `linkGeneration`, `installPackages` and `reloadSystemd` but *before* `zen-browser-default` and `zenInstallsIni`, the resulting state is:

- `~/.local/state/nix/profiles/home-manager` **already points at the new generation** (the CLI set it before calling `activate`), so `home-manager generations` reports the new generation as `(current)` and `$PATH` reflects it.
- All files are linked and all packages installed.
- `gcroots/current-home` **still points at the old generation**. On the next `hms`, `oldGenPath` is therefore the *old* generation, so `linkGeneration`'s orphan cleanup and `checkFilesChanged`/`onFilesChange` diff against a stale file list: any path that the failed generation added and the next one drops is never unlinked. That is a silent, persistent divergence, not a one-shot failure.
- `zenInstallsIni` never runs — so `installs.ini` survives and Zen re-pins its own `*.default-release` profile on next launch. That is precisely the bug `home.nix:1757-1767` exists to prevent, silently reintroduced by an unrelated `steam.desktop` write failure. `zen-browser-default` is also skipped.
- `presentNews` is skipped (cosmetic).

On the consistency question you asked: this entry is consistent *in form* with the repo's others (none use `|| true`), but not *in consequence*. `zenInstallsIni` is a bare `rm -f` on a path whose parent is writable — it essentially cannot fail. `opencodeConfig` / `piModelsConfig` / `piSettings` can fail, and aborting there is arguably right: a missing `opencode.json` or `models.json` means the tool has no provider at all, so failing loudly beats proceeding. `steamDesktopOverride` is not in that class. Its worst-case degraded outcome is "Steam launches via `/usr/bin/steam` instead of the wrapper", i.e. the download-directory bug comes back — annoying, recoverable, and strictly better than an aborted switch with the bookkeeping above. **Best-effort-with-a-warning is the right policy for this one entry, and abort is not.** Concretely: wrap the invocation so failure is visible but non-fatal, e.g.

```
$DRY_RUN_CMD ${pkgs.bash}/bin/bash ${steam-desktop-override} … \
  || warnEcho "steamDesktopOverride: failed; Steam will launch unwrapped"
```

(`warnEcho`/`errorEcho` are available from `initHomeManagerLib`, which `activate` sources — so the message lands in hm's own output format rather than being swallowed.) If you keep the abort, that choice deserves to be argued in the comment block, because right now the comment discusses the *success* no-op path at length and says nothing about the failure path.

---

## Important

**I1. `[ -r "$src" ] || exit 0` conflates "this host has no Steam" with "Steam is here but its desktop file moved", and in the second case it leaves a stale override in place forever.**

Two distinct bad states:

- *Silent stop.* If a pacman update renames/relocates `steam.desktop`, or ships it under a different path, the gate fires, the script exits 0, nothing is printed, and launches quietly go back to `/usr/bin/steam` — reintroducing the exact `xdg-user-dir` glibc crash this change exists to fix. There is no signal at all. The repo's own precedent for "is it installed" is `pacman -Qq thermald` (`system/thermald-setup:40`), which *does* distinguish the two; the script's comment claims it uses "the same split" as thermald-setup, but the gate is materially weaker.
- *Stale override.* If `steam` is removed from `system/packages.shiori`, or from `home.packages` in `home.nix`, `$dst` is never touched again. `~/.local/share/applications/steam.desktop` persists with `Exec=/nix/store/<old-hash>-steam/bin/steam %U`, and because `XDG_DATA_HOME` outranks `/usr/share` it **shadows** the packaged entry. Once old generations expire and GC runs, that store path is gone: clicking Steam in elephant/walker does nothing visible (stderr goes to the journal, not to the user), and `x-scheme-handler/steam` resolves to a `.desktop` whose `Exec` is a dead path. This is the specific robustness property given up by choosing an activation entry over `xdg.dataFile` — hm's `linkGeneration` removes its own orphans; this file has no owner and no removal path.

Both are fixed by the same one-liner: make the "no source" branch a cleanup branch rather than a bare `exit 0` —

```
[ -r "$src" ] || { rm -f "$dst"; exit 0; }
```

and, if you want the silent-stop signal, also emit a warning when the host is one where Steam is expected.

**I2. No post-condition check on the rewrite: a source whose `Exec=` shape changed produces a shadowing passthrough copy, silently.**

The two anchored patterns match today's file exactly (verified: 10 lines). If a future `steam` package writes `Exec=steam %U`, `Exec=/usr/bin/steam-runtime …`, adds a leading space, or the file is read while truncated, `sed` matches nothing, exits 0, and `mv` installs a file at a path that **outranks** `/usr/share/applications/steam.desktop` — so you get an override that either bypasses the wrapper entirely (no-match case) or is empty/truncated, making Steam vanish from the launcher and `steam://` stop resolving. Nothing in the script or the tests would notice. The whole justification for deriving the file from the pacman copy instead of vendoring it (`home/steam-desktop-override:10-15`) is "a package update is picked up rather than drifting silently" — but the *failure* of that derivation is exactly as silent as the drift it replaces. Two cheap guards close it:

```
[ -s "$tmp" ] || { echo "$0: refusing to install an empty override" >&2; exit 1; }
grep -q "^Exec=$exe" "$tmp" || { echo "$0: no Exec= line matched in $src — upstream format changed?" >&2; exit 1; }
```

(with C1's `|| warnEcho` in place, these become loud-but-non-fatal, which is the behaviour you want.)

**I3. `set -u` + `$PATH` in the wrapper: the wrapper crashes instead of launching Steam if `PATH` is unset in the parent environment, and the test harness structurally cannot catch it.**

`export PATH="/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:$PATH"` under `set -u` aborts with `PATH: unbound variable`, exit 1, if `PATH` is not in the environment. Practically rare (dbus/systemd activation normally carries `PATH`), but the wrapper is the single chokepoint between every launcher and Steam, and the cost of `${PATH:+:}${PATH:-}` or `${PATH:-}` is one token. Worth noting that `tests/steam-env.sh:run()` always passes `PATH=…` through `env -i`, so this is not merely untested — it is untestable in the harness as written, while the harness's own comment advertises "a deliberately hostile parent environment".

**I4. The production `STEAM_BIN` default — the only value that ever runs on the real host — is asserted by zero of the 26 cases.**

Every case goes through `run()`, which sets `STEAM_BIN="$D/stub"`. So `${STEAM_BIN:-/usr/bin/steam}` has its *seam* exercised and its *default* never. Changing the default to `/usr/local/bin/steam`, `/usr/lib/steam/steam`, or dropping the `:-` entirely (making it a `set -u` abort) passes all 26 cases. One case with `STEAM_BIN` unset, asserting the failure message names `/usr/bin/steam` (or asserting against a fake root), closes it.

**I5. The activation call site is untested — a wrong `$dst` produces an override that silently never applies.**

`tests/steam-env.sh` drives the script directly and the wrapper directly, but nothing asserts that `home.activation.steamDesktopOverride` passes the right three arguments. A typo that sent `$dst` to `${config.xdg.dataHome}/applications/Steam.desktop` (wrong case), or to the profile's `share/applications` — the directory `home.nix:1943` and `home.nix:1966-1970` both specifically warn *loses* to `/usr/share` — passes all 26 cases and produces zero user-visible effect. `tests/steam-ui-scaling.sh` already establishes the idiom for this (`nix eval --json "$FLAKE#homeConfigurations.$1.config.$2"`); `config.home.activation.steamDesktopOverride.data` is a string you can grep for the three paths.

**I6. "re-running is idempotent" passes for the wrong reason on a real regression.**

```bash
before=$(cat "$out")
bash "$OVERRIDE" "$D/steam.desktop" "$out" "$W" 2>/dev/null
if [ "$before" = "$(cat "$out")" ]; then ok "re-running is idempotent"
